fields.quote: Post-write deletion removes cache fills that finish during the write, but an older in-flight snapshot can refill the cache afterward.
fields.rationale: after.fillDuringWrite: overlappingRead "old", cached null, nextRead "new", matching probe.mjs assert equal(results.after.fillDuringWrite.nextRead, "new"). after.lateSnapshot: cached "old", nextRead "old", matching assert equal(result.lateSnapshot.cached, "old") and nextRead "old". Contract: db.read captures a snapshot when invoked and may fulfill after a later write commits.

fields.quote: Early deletion left a window for stale fills
fields.rationale: source.before deletes before await db.write. before.fillDuringWrite overlappingRead, cached, and nextRead are all "old". Probe assert equal(results.before.fillDuringWrite.nextRead, "old").

fields.quote: The old update deleted the cached entry before awaiting the database write. A cache miss could read and cache the old stored value during that wait.
fields.rationale: source.before / functions.mjs before: cache.delete(key) then await db.write. overlapping(fn, false) starts the write, then read on an empty Map, so db.read snapshots stored while it is still "old", cache.set of that value, then the write commits. before.fillDuringWrite: overlappingRead "old", cached "old".
Section label only. No checkable claim.

fields.quote: Delete only after the write fulfills
fields.rationale: source.after / functions.mjs after: await db.write then cache.delete. Contract: db.write commits before fulfillment; rejection leaves the stored value unchanged. after.failedWrite: error "write", cachedAfterUpdate "old" (delete does not run). after.sequential: cachedAfterUpdate null after a successful write.

fields.quote: The changed update deletes after the write succeeds. It removes an old cache fill that completed during the write. A failed write leaves an existing cached entry in place. In the sequential example, the next read sees the new stored value.
fields.rationale: after() deletes only after await db.write. after.fillDuringWrite.cached is null and nextRead is "new" (fill during write is deleted). sequential(fn, true) starts from Map([['key','old']]); after.failedWrite.cachedAfterUpdate is "old". after.sequential.nextRead is "new". The last sentence is scoped to that sequential example; the same nextRead "new" also appears for before.sequential, so it is true of after but not distinctive.
Section label only. No checkable claim.

fields.quote: An older snapshot can arrive after deletion
fields.rationale: overlapping(fn, true): read snapshots stored while it is "old", the update commits and deletes, then the reader is released and cache.set writes that snapshot. after.lateSnapshot: stored "new", cached "old", nextRead "old".

fields.rationale: source.body: the author says invalidating after the write removes stale cache reads, including concurrent readers. source.unchanged and contract: read is unchanged; no generation check or in-flight reader synchronization. lateSnapshot path matches the modeled reader; after.lateSnapshot.nextRead is "old". The author paraphrase is narrower than source.body (which also claimed stale cache reads in general) but is not contradicted by the source sentence.

fields.quote: Moving deletion after a successful write closes the window for fills that finish during that write. It does not prevent stale results from overlapping readers or late cache fills.
